newsitem.title: USA: Ecopetrol force majeures Cano Limon cargoes-trader.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol force majeures Cano Limon cargoes-trader.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol declared force majeure on loadings of Cano Limon crude oil in the wake of yet another string of rebel attacks on the Cano Limon-Coveas pipeline, a trade source said on Tuesday.
Cargoes are expected to be delayed by about five days from their original loading dates, the source said.
The emergency measure took effect either sometime over the weekend or early on Monday.
A major U.S. oil company had a cargo scheduled to load August 6-8. The tanker is not expected to load until next week as a result of the disruption, the source said.
The 250,000-300,000 barrel per day (bpd) pipeline running to the Caribbean port of Coveas has been attacked 45 times so far this year, as many times as all of last year.
"The attacks are getting more frequent and more severe," the source said.
The recent attacks also prompted field operator Occidental Petroleum Inc to declare force majeure on Monday on the 175,000 bpd Cano Limon field.
This is the second declaration of force majeure on both loadings and field operations within a month, raising new questions about security in Colombia's growing oil industry.
The attacks are thought to be the work of the National Liberation Army (ELN), one of the main guerrilla groups operating in Colombia.
